analysis:
Examined the only change in SSDPrefixCache.swift: retireIndexedEntries (head ~1793-1802) now calls SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices(urls) and takes removalLock per slice instead of once for the whole batch. The per-slice closure keeps the same guard (hasSafeRoot && ownsEvictionRoot) and the same SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove(urls:root:index:epochStore:) call, so path-safety and epoch ownership checks are rechecked on every slice. The external-change reconcile still follows the call. This appears to be an availability/lock-hold-time improvement (relevant to T-041 cache disk/TTL/LRU cleanup) with no new data exposure, no change to crypto (DBK3/AES-GCM/HMAC tags), TTL, scope, or the KEK purge path.

Unverified because removeInSlices and the Result merge semantics are outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should check: (1) that the nil-returning closure (not owned or unsafe root) stops iteration or yields an empty result rather than continuing with stale state; (2) that Result merging across slices keeps externalChange, removed and indexedBytesFreed correct, since evictOldestEntry (~1777-1785) relies on externalChange and indexedBytesFreed; (3) that a concurrent donation or stage between slices cannot see index/file inconsistencies, since the removal barrier is no longer held across the whole batch. performExternalDestructiveChange and performIndexedRemoval were not changed here. No finding is supported by the supplied evidence, but the unseen helper leaves some uncertainty.
